{{nihongo|'''Toyoyuki Shrine'''|豐由氣神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Suruga Province]].

'''Toyoyuki Shrine''' (とよゆけじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ihara-chō}}, {{ill|Shimizu-ku, Shizuoka|Q79385|qid=Q79385}}, {{ill|Shizuoka (city)|Q174691|qid=Q174691}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}. Its former rank in the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Outline ===
The founding is unknown. It stands directly south of the {{ill|Ihara District, Shizuoka|Q988501|qid=Q988501|lt=Ihara}} {{ill|Kofun cluster|Q11411019|qid=Q11411019}}.

In {{ill|2005|Q2019|qid=Q2019}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 17), construction of {{ill|Shizuoka City Shimizu Ihara Ballpark|Q11662968|qid=Q11662968}} caused the loss of much of the kofun group, but shrine rites continue. It is also an old shrine connected with the {{ill|Ihara no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Q11486229|qid=Q11486229|lt=Ihara no Kuni no Miyatsuko}}.

The shrine architecture shows similarities with {{ill|Shizuoka Sengen Shrine|Q500368|qid=Q500368}}. It is {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} with copper roofing.

The {{ill|Setsumatsusha|Q1071160|qid=Q1071160|lt=subsidiary shrine}} Shinmei-gū follows the style of {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Keku|zh|豐受大神宮|qid=Q11633343|lt=Gekū}}. It is a small shrine enshrining seven deities of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|Q11581011|qid=Q11581011|lt=Naikū}} and {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Keku|zh|豐受大神宮|qid=Q11633343|lt=Gekū}}.
